title: Optimized Quantum States for Sensing in the Presence of Loss and Phase Noise
authors: Shruti Maliakal, Zachary Mann, Christopher Wipf, Rana X Adhikari, Su Direkci, Yanbei Chen
abstract: Squeezed vacuum lets gravitational-wave detectors and other quantum sensors surpass the standard quantum limit, and is optimal in the loss-limited regime; phase noise breaks this optimality. Numerically optimizing the quantum Fisher information across the loss and phase-noise landscape, we identify non-Gaussian states that outperform any Gaussian state. These fall into three classes: Fock-like, cubic-phase-like, and states with discrete rotational symmetry. Limiting the average number of photons in the input state to $\bar{n}=5$, with $1-η= 5\%$ photon loss and 200 mrad phase noise, the non-Gaussian advantage reaches up to 2.2 dB. Furthermore, we observe that the non-Gaussian advantage can persist even when the measurement strategy is homodyne detection.
summary: This theoretical study optimizes quantum states for enhanced sensing in noisy environments characterized by photon loss and phase noise. By numerically maximizing the Quantum Fisher Information, the authors prove that non-Gaussian states surpass Gaussian limits, achieving measurable advantages up to 2.2 dB under realistic conditions. The work is crucial for advancing practical quantum measurement techniques.
main_problem: The research aims to enhance quantum sensing sensitivity beyond the standard quantum limit (SQL) when the system is corrupted by both photon loss and phase noise.
main_result: Non-Gaussian states, specifically Fock-like, cubic-phase-like, and discrete rotational symmetry states, were found to outperform all Gaussian states, achieving up to a 2.2 dB non-Gaussian advantage under specific noisy conditions.
method: The authors used numerical optimization techniques to maximize the Quantum Fisher Information (QFI) across various input state ansatze while incorporating Lindblad operators for loss and phase noise.
model_or_system: The system models quantum metrology, relevant to gravitational-wave detectors. The dynamics are governed by a Hamiltonian subject to amplitude damping (loss) and dephasing (phase noise).
key_observables: Quantum Fisher Information (QFI), Non-Gaussian Advantage (in dB), Classical Fisher Information (CFI), Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) gain.
important_parameters: Average photon number ($ ar{n}$), Photon loss ($1-\eta$), Phase noise standard deviation ($\sigma_\phi$).
main_assumptions: The analysis compares QFI derived from optimal measurements against those achievable with specific, experimentally relevant readouts like homodyne detection.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the non-Gaussian advantage across parameter grids $(\eta, \sigma_\phi)$, show Wigner function evolution, and compare CFI gains for different measurement types (PNR vs. Homodyne).
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the optimal state class by mapping out regions in the loss/noise parameter space where Fock-like, cubic-phase-like, or rotationally symmetric states yield the maximum QFI advantage.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses open quantum systems and quantum optics by providing concrete, non-Gaussian resource states that maintain quantum advantages even when realistic noise channels (loss/dephasing) are present. The comparison between QFI and CFI is particularly insightful for experimentalists.
